Front: What is a URL shortener?
Back: A service that maps a long URL to a short alias (e.g. 7 chars). When a user visits the short URL they are redirected to the original. Examples: TinyURL / Bit.ly / goo.gl / t.co.

Front: What are the two core operations of a URL shortener?
Back: 1) URL Shortening: POST longURL → receive shortURL. 2) URL Redirecting: GET shortURL → 301/302 redirect to longURL.

Front: Why is n=7 the minimum hash length for a URL shortener supporting 365B URLs?
Back: 62^7 = 3.5 trillion. Covers 365B needed with a 10× safety margin. 62^6 = 56.8B which is insufficient.

Front: What character set does Base62 use and why not Base64?
Back: Base62: 0-9 + a-z + A-Z (62 chars). Base64 adds + / = which are URL-unsafe and require percent-encoding — defeating the 'short' purpose.

Front: What is the difference between 301 and 302 HTTP redirects in the context of URL shorteners?
Back: 301 = Permanent: browser caches, bypasses server, reduces load, but can't track clicks. 302 = Temporary: browser always hits server, allows analytics tracking. Use 302 when analytics needed.

Front: When should you use 301 vs 302 for URL shortening?
Back: Use 302 when analytics/click tracking is needed (most commercial URL shorteners). Use 301 when minimizing server load is the priority and analytics don't matter. The answer is: it depends on requirements.

Front: What is the URL shortening API endpoint design?
Back: POST /api/v1/data/shorten with body {longUrl: '...'} → returns {shortUrl: '...'}. Authenticated via API key. Rate limited.

Front: What is the URL redirecting API endpoint design?
Back: GET /api/v1/{shortUrl} → returns 301 or 302 with Location header pointing to longUrl. Returns 404 if not found.

Front: What is the URL table schema for a URL shortener?
Back: CREATE TABLE url (id BIGINT PK AUTO_INCREMENT, short_url VARCHAR(7) UNIQUE, long_url TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMP, expiry_date TIMESTAMP NULL). Index on both short_url and long_url.

Front: Why index the long_url column in the URL table?
Back: To support idempotency checks: SELECT short_url WHERE long_url = ? This allows returning the existing shortURL when the same longURL is submitted again.

Front: What are the two approaches to generating shortURLs?
Back: 1) Hash + Collision Resolution: apply MD5/SHA-1 to longURL, take first 7 chars, resolve collisions. 2) Base62 Conversion: generate unique auto-increment ID, convert to Base62 string.

Front: What is the hash + collision resolution algorithm for URL shortening?
Back: hash = MD5(longURL)[:7]; if collision: append predefined salt to longURL and rehash. Use Bloom filter to avoid DB lookup on each new URL: if Bloom says 'not exists' → safe to insert without DB read.

Front: What is a Bloom filter and how does it help with collision resolution?
Back: A probabilistic data structure. Lookup result: 'definitely NOT in set' (no false negatives) or 'probably in set' (false positives possible). For URL shortener: if Bloom says 'not exists', skip DB read. Only query DB on 'probably exists'. Eliminates most DB reads.

Front: What are the four possible Bloom filter outcomes?
Back: True negative: not in set, says not in set (100% accurate). True positive: in set, says in set. False positive: not in set, says in set (possible). False negative: in set, says not in set (IMPOSSIBLE — this is the key guarantee).

Front: What is the Base62 conversion algorithm?
Back: Convert integer ID to base-62 string using chars [0-9a-zA-Z]. Repeatedly: result = CHARS[id % 62]; id //= 62. Reverse result and pad to 7 chars. No collision possible since each ID is unique.

Compare Hash+Collision vs Base62 for URL shortening
Back: Hash: can collide (must detect), no ID gen needed, harder to enumerate. Base62: no collision, needs distributed ID generator, sequential IDs are guessable. Hash is more private; Base62 is simpler logic.

Front: Why are Base62-generated shortURLs a security concern?
Back: They're based on sequential IDs which can be guessed/enumerated. An attacker can crawl all short URLs by incrementing. Mitigations: use hash-based approach
column3: or add random salt before Base62 encoding.

Front: What is Twitter Snowflake and why use it for URL shortening?
Back: 64-bit ID = 41-bit timestamp + 10-bit machine ID + 12-bit sequence. Generates 4096 unique IDs/ms per machine. Distributed, no central coordinator, time-sorted. Best choice for Base62 ID generation at scale.

Front: What is the URL shortening flow (Figure 8-7)?
Back: 1) Client POSTs longURL. 2) Check DB for existing longURL (idempotency). 3) If new: get ID from ID generator. 4) Convert ID to Base62. 5) Save {id, shortURL, longURL} to DB. 6) Add to cache. 7) Return shortURL.

Front: What is the URL redirecting flow (Figure 8-8)?
Back: 1) Client GETs shortURL. 2) Load Balancer routes to web server. 3) Web server checks Redis cache. 4) Cache HIT: return 301/302 immediately. 5) Cache MISS: query DB, populate cache, return 301/302. 6) Return 404 if not found.

Front: How do you handle idempotency when the same longURL is submitted twice?
Back: Option A (recommended): Check long_url index first. Return existing shortURL if found. Handle race condition with DB UNIQUE constraint on long_url + retry on violation. Option B: Always create new (wastes storage, confusing UX).

Front: How do you size the Redis cache for URL shortening?
Back: Top 10% of daily active URLs: 100M × 10% = 10M entries. At ~500 bytes/entry = 5 GB. Fits in a single Redis node. Use LRU eviction.

Front: What is the Pareto principle applied to URL redirecting?
Back: 20% of URLs get 80% of traffic. Top 10% cached in Redis → ~80% cache hit rate → only ~20% of redirect requests hit the database.

Front: How do you scale the URL shortener database?
Back: 1) Add read replicas (redirect reads are 10× more than writes). 2) Vertical scaling short-term. 3) Horizontal sharding by shortURL hash prefix. 4) Migrate to NoSQL (DynamoDB/Cassandra) for pure key-value access.

Front: Why is NoSQL a natural fit for URL shortening?
Back: Access pattern is pure key-value: shortURL → longURL. No joins
column3: no complex queries. DynamoDB/Cassandra scale horizontally with shortURL as partition key. Trade-off: lose SQL features and auto-increment ID.

Front: What consistency model is needed for URL shortening vs redirecting?
Back: Creation (writes): strong consistency — two simultaneous creates must not produce the same shortURL. Redirecting (reads): eventual consistency OK — stale cache gives old destination for a few seconds, usually acceptable.

Front: What is a race condition in URL creation and how do you handle it?
Back: Two requests submit the same longURL simultaneously. Both pass the idempotency check before either writes. Solution: DB UNIQUE constraint on long_url. Handle constraint violation by returning the existing record.

Front: How do you add analytics without slowing down redirects?
Back: Publish click event to message queue asynchronously (non-blocking) during redirect handler. Separate analytics consumer processes events. Adds <1ms latency vs direct DB write adding 5-20ms.

Front: What does an analytics event payload look like for URL shortening?
Back: { short_url, long_url, timestamp, user_agent, ip_address, referer }. Consumed by analytics pipeline to compute: total clicks, unique visitors, geo-distribution, device breakdown, referrer sources.

Front: How would you support custom aliases (vanity URLs)?
Back: Separate vanity_url table with user_id foreign key. Validate against reserved words (api www admin). Check availability endpoint. Premium feature with rate limits. Validate alphanumeric-only

Front: What happens when a shortURL expires?
Back: Return 410 Gone (not 404). 410 means 'resource intentionally removed'. Store expiry_date in url table. Background job (cron or TTL-based) cleans up expired entries and invalidates cache.

Front: How do you prevent phishing abuse of URL shorteners?
Back: Scan destination URL against Google Safe Browsing API on creation. Maintain internal blocklist of known malicious domains. Show interstitial warning page before redirecting. Enable user reporting.

Front: What are the non-functional requirements for a URL shortener?
Back: High availability (redirects must never fail). Low latency (<100ms redirect). Scalability (viral link spikes). Durability (short URLs must not break). Unpredictability (not easily enumerable).

Front: Why can't you use UUID for the shortURL directly?
Back: 128-bit UUID in Base62 = ~22 chars. Too long for a 'short' URL. Truncating UUID reintroduces collision risk. Better: use a dedicated ID generator (Snowflake) that produces smaller IDs.

Front: What is the 62^n formula and what n should you pick for 10 years at 100M/day?
Back: Need to cover 365B URLs. 62^6 = 56.8B (too small). 62^7 = 3.5T (covers 365B with 10× safety margin). Answer: n = 7.

Front: What is the rate limiting strategy for a URL shortener?
Back: Token bucket or leaky bucket per API key. Example: 100 URL creations per minute per API key. IP-based fallback for unauthenticated users. 429 Too Many Requests response with Retry-After header.

Front: What is the difference between a URL shortener and a URL redirector?
Back: URL shortener creates a new short alias and stores the mapping. URL redirector just redirects — no storage needed. A full URL shortener service includes: creation endpoint, redirect endpoint, analytics, expiry, abuse prevention.
